features.headline: Miami Heat players receive GTA VI care packages from Rockstar Games
features.desc: Heat players received a custom game-themed care package complete with custom controllers, consoles and, of course, a copy of the game.
body: Players around the NBA are gearing up for "Grand Theft Auto VI," but some are going to be particularly ready for the game's highly anticipated Thursday release: Miami Heat players.
Unsurprisingly for a team that has been meticulously embracing Vice City branding for years — "Grand Theft Auto: Vice City,"

the fourth game in the series first introduced in 2002, is set in a fictional city based on Miami, which GTA VI will return to — the Heat are rolling out an impressive promotion ahead of GTA VI going live. Wednesday will be "A Night in Vice City"
at the Kaseya Center, featuring a new court design, concessions and more.
But the promotional street runs both ways — and Miami Heat players are reaping the benefits.

A number of players, including Davion Mitchell, Nick Richards, Tim Hardaway Jr. and more posted about receiving a custom game-themed care package from Rockstar Games, PlayStation and luggage company Rimowa for GTA VI's release — complete with custom controllers, consoles and, of course, a copy of the game.
The care package came in a fitting color scheme — Miami's Vice City pink and black alternate branding.
Mitchell, who posted about the gift on his Instagram story, added a humorous caption:
"I'm about to deactivate my account because I'm about to lock in," he wrote, adding saluting and laughing emojis. "It's up!!!"
The Heat will face the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday night (7 p.m. EST, ESPN).

features.headline: 2026-27 MLB free agency, trade grades: Offseason analysis
features.desc: We've got you covered with grades and analysis on every winter signing and big offseason trade.
body: The 2026-27 MLB offseason is officially here, and we have you covered with grades and analysis for every major signing and trade as this winter — which is expected to include a labor stoppage — unfolds.
Whether it's a franchise-changing free agent signing or an unexpected blockbuster trade, we'll weigh in with what it all means for next season and beyond.

ESPN MLB experts Bradford Doolittle and David Schoenfield will evaluate each move as it happens, so follow along here — this story will continue to be updated. Check back in for all the most recent analysis.
Seattle Mariners get: IF Maikel Garcia RHP James McArthur RHP L.P. Langevin
Kansas City Royals get: RHP Bryce Miller RHP Logan Evans LHP Jose Ferrer
Garcia is the best player in the deal and the difference is enough to make this a slam-dunk win for Seattle.

Nagging injuries undermined Garcia's 2026 season after his breakout the year before, but even so, his contract and patience at the plate remained well above average and he remained one of baseball's top defensive third basemen.
While the injuries cost him in the power department and on the bases, Garcia is entering his age-27 season as a good bet to bounce back to All-Star form.
His well-documented penchant for self-improvement also supports the argument for positive regression.
Under contract through 2031 on team-friendly terms, Garcia is a major upgrade at a soft spot on the Mariners' depth chart.
Seattle's defensive projection at the hot corner leaped from 21st to first in my system, and the offensive leap in runs from that spot was about 10 spots, to No. 12.

features.headline: MLB free agency tracker: 2026-27 offseason trades, moves
features.desc: We've got you covered on all the major MLB hot stove signings and trades.
body: The 2026-27 MLB hot stove was lit just days after the Milwaukee Brewers hoisted the franchise's first World Series championship trophy.

All eyes this winter are on the free agency of two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal. But he's not the only one who will make a splash in the market, with Freddya Peralta, Randy Arozarena, Seiya Suzuki and Michael King among the other free agents to watch.
Which teams will go big to contend for the 2027 World Series title? And who will make the trades and signings that have everyone buzzing?
Below is a running list of notable transactions and updates from throughout the MLB offseason.

The Seattle Mariners are acquiring Gold Glove third baseman Maikel Garcia in a six-player trade with the Kansas City Royals, sources tell ESPN. The Royals are receiving three major league pitchers in return, headlined by right-hander Bryce Miller.
The Chicago White Sox are in agreement with free agent pitcher Dustin May on a three-year, $52.5 million deal, source confirms to ESPN.
Left-hander Tim Hill is staying with the New York Yankees, agreeing to a one-year, $2.25 million contract, sources told ESPN's Jeff Passan.
Reliever Ryan Walker went to the Milwaukee Brewers in a trade that sent right-handers Blake Holub and Gavin Perry to the San Francisco Giants.
First baseman Jake Bauers and the Boston Red Sox are in agreement on a four-year, $58 million contract, sources tell ESPN.
Reliever Evan Phillips and the Atlanta Braves are in agreement on a three-year, $35 million contract.

features.headline: Facts vs. Feelings: Bye-mageddon means getting comfortable with the uncomfortable
features.desc: A bye-laden Week 11 might make you cringe at some of your lineup decisions, so let the facts hone your feelings on Bo Nix, Tony Pollard, Jaylen Warren, Chris Olave, Malik Nabers, Stefon Diggs and Colston Loveland.
body: Employing the crying laughing emoji (officially named Face with Tears of Joy) with unabashed enthusiasm.
Telling a perfect stranger you like their shoes.
Gasping with delight at the sight of livestock roaming near the roadside.

A verb that once described the action of drawing back or recoiling in fear, disgust or pain has since morphed into a standalone adjective (or noun) used to describe anything that causes secondhand embarrassment or comes across as awkward.

But to whom? Who exactly is so deeply troubled by these random acts of mirth? Maybe I've been too busy sorting aDOT and YAC (yikes) to notice, but has a single person or, perhaps, a coalition of judges been appointed as the Official Arbiters of Taste?
Given how much "cringe" is referenced, I imagine there must exist a chronically online task force set up to systematically stamp out any whimsy, frivolity and/or earnestness.
After all, the only thing worse than being a try-hard is to actually try hard at something.

I don't clap when the plane lands. But two months ago, I sat next to a young woman who did her best "When Harry Met Sally" impression and let out a boisterous, "OH, THANK GOD!" the second we touched down at O'Hare.

My dated movie reference aside, her outburst genuinely amused me. Was it cringe? Sure. Still, I bet the flight crew was deeply touched when she personally thanked every single one of them for helping her overcome a crippling fear of flying.
Have we become so afraid of looking foolish that we've stopped expressing delight... or worse, stopped feeling it altogether?

features.headline: Tarik Skubal free agency tracker: Latest on top MLB free agent
features.desc: Who will land the two-time Cy Young Award winner? We have all the latest updates on where things stand.
body: All eyes are on ace Tarik Skubal as MLB free agency gets underway ahead of the impending labor stoppage.

The current collective bargaining agreement expires on Dec. 1, meaning that after that, no players can sign until a new CBA is established. This could put Skubal on the fast track to a new contract, as many around the sport expect him to sign ahead of the lockout.
Where do things currently stand in Skubal's free agency? What's the latest? We have everything you need to know about the winter's No. 1 free agent in one place.
Skubal met with the New York Mets on Monday and the Los Angeles Dodgers and Toronto Blue Jays on Tuesday. He is expected to round out his in-person get-togethers with the San Diego Padres this week.
By the time he signs — and it could be sooner than later — it will be the largest deal for a pitcher in baseball history. Read more in Jeff Passan's MLB free agency preview
Nov. 16: The Tarik Skubal Tiers: We break all 30 teams into tiers based on their likelihood of landing the prize of this free agent class, along with a reasonable backup pitching plan for each.

Nov. 11: Passan's perfect move for top contenders: Skubal has no interest in a shorter-term, higher-dollar deal, which could disadvantage the Dodgers. The Mets could be in the strongest position to land Skubal this offseason.
Nov. 10: Mets to meet with prized ace Skubal next week: The Mets have a need for front-line starting pitching and an owner in Steve Cohen who's willing to spend.
